chunks: From Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah the Exalted did not grant Satan authority over those who have faith.
But [He granted authority] over those who take him as their guardian and disobey His command.

key_terms.يَتَوَلَّوْنَهُمْ: Those who take him as guardian/ally

ai.seo_question: Who does Satan have authority over according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq’s (a) clarification that Satan’s *sultan* (authority) is conditional upon human free will, specifically applying to those who voluntarily follow his whispers. This distinction refutes the notion of absolute demonic dominion, emphasizing that believers retain agency to resist through conscious obedience to God. The narration underscores the Shia theological principle that spiritual subjugation is a result of choice, not predestination.
